paragraphs.title: The Dream and the Impossible Demand

easy.explanation: Nebuchadnezzar dreamed the dreams.
easy.q: Who dreamed the dreams?

answers: The magicians, astrologers, sorcerers, and Chaldeans
easy.explanation: The king called Babylon’s wise men.
easy.q: Whom did the king command to call?

answers: That they interpret only the dream
That they tell the dream and its interpretation
easy.explanation: He demanded both the dream and its interpretation.
easy.q: What did the king demand from the wise men?

answers: They did not know the dream
The king had left the palace
medium.explanation: The king had not told them the dream.
medium.q: Why were the wise men troubled by the king’s demand?

answers: They would be cut in pieces and their houses made a dunghill
medium.explanation: The king threatened them with death and destruction.
medium.q: What would happen if the wise men could not tell the king the dream and its interpretation?

answers: A heap of refuse or manure
medium.explanation: A dunghill is a heap of waste or manure.
medium.q: What does the KJV word “dunghill” mean in this passage?

answers: That they were trying to gain time
That they wanted to help Daniel
That they had forgotten Babylon’s language
challenge.explanation: The king suspected that they were trying to delay him.
challenge.q: What suspicion did the king have about the Chaldeans?

answers: It was a normal request from every king
No man on earth could reveal such a thing
challenge.explanation: They said no man on earth could show the king’s matter.
challenge.q: What did the Chaldeans say about the king’s demand?

answers: They were among Babylon’s wise men
They refused to serve the king
They asked to punish the Chaldeans
challenge.explanation: The decree against the wise men included Daniel and his companions.
challenge.q: Why did the decree include Daniel and his companions?

easy.explanation: Daniel spoke to Arioch, the king’s captain.
easy.q: With whom did Daniel speak after learning about the decree?

easy.explanation: Daniel asked for time to show the interpretation.
easy.q: What did Daniel ask the king to give him?

easy.explanation: They sought mercies from the God of heaven.
easy.q: To whom did Daniel and his companions turn for help?

answers: He asked the king for time
He claimed to know the interpretation
medium.explanation: Daniel asked for time to show the king the interpretation.
medium.q: What did Daniel do after Arioch told him about the decree?

answers: So they could seek mercy together
So they could flee the city
So they could interpret the dream alone
medium.explanation: Daniel wanted them to seek God together concerning the secret.
medium.q: Why did Daniel tell Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah about the danger?

medium.explanation: They were asking God for mercy and help.
medium.q: What does “mercies” mean in “they would desire mercies of the God of heaven”?

answers: He acted wisely rather than rashly
He only wanted to delay punishment
challenge.explanation: Daniel stopped the immediate action and sought time to respond wisely.
challenge.q: What does Daniel’s request for time show about how he faced danger?

answers: The time allowed Daniel and his companions to seek God for the revelation
The prayer was meant to cancel the request for time
challenge.explanation: After receiving time, they sought mercy from God concerning the secret.
challenge.q: What was the connection between the request for time and prayer?

answers: Being destroyed with Babylon’s wise men
challenge.explanation: They sought not to perish with the other wise men.
challenge.q: From what danger did Daniel and his companions seek deliverance?

paragraphs.title: The Secret Revealed and God Praised

answers: By a letter from the king
easy.explanation: The secret was revealed in a night vision.
easy.q: How was the secret revealed to Daniel?

answers: He blessed the God of heaven
He became angry with the Chaldeans
easy.explanation: Daniel blessed God after receiving the revelation.
easy.q: What did Daniel do after the secret was revealed?

easy.explanation: Daniel said that wisdom and might are God’s.
easy.q: To whom do wisdom and might belong?

answers: Only the names of the wise men
medium.explanation: The KJV says that God reveals the deep and secret things.
medium.q: What hidden things can God reveal?

medium.explanation: Daniel credited God with wisdom, might, and revelation.
medium.q: What does Daniel’s praise teach about the source of his ability?

answers: God gave him wisdom and made the king’s matter known
The king gave him a house
medium.explanation: Daniel thanked God for wisdom and for revealing the king’s matter.
medium.q: Why did Daniel thank God after learning the secret?

answers: God knows what is in darkness, and light dwells with Him
challenge.explanation: God knows what is in darkness, and light dwells with Him.
challenge.q: What relationship between light and darkness does Daniel describe?

challenge.explanation: God is presented as sovereign over times and rulers.
challenge.q: What does God’s changing times and seasons and removing and setting up kings show?

answers: He discovered it by his own wisdom
The revelation was God’s grace, not merely his personal achievement
The king told it to him
challenge.explanation: Daniel acknowledged that God made the revelation known.
challenge.q: What does Daniel emphasize by saying that the secret was revealed to him?

answers: Not to destroy Babylon’s wise men
easy.explanation: Daniel told Arioch not to destroy the wise men.
easy.q: What did Daniel ask Arioch to do?

easy.explanation: The king called Daniel Belteshazzar.
easy.q: By what name was Daniel known to the king?

answers: They could not reveal the secret
easy.explanation: Daniel said the wise men could not show the secret.
easy.q: What did Daniel say about Babylon’s wise men?

answers: He was found able to make the interpretation known
He was commander of the army
He wanted to replace the king
medium.explanation: Arioch brought Daniel as one who could reveal the interpretation.
medium.q: Why was Daniel brought before the king?

answers: He was wiser than everyone else
The secret did not come from his own wisdom
medium.explanation: Daniel said the secret was not revealed to him because of superior personal wisdom.
medium.q: What did Daniel emphasize before revealing the secret?

answers: People taken away from their homeland
medium.explanation: Daniel was one of the people taken captive from Judah.
medium.q: What does the KJV word “captives” mean in “a man of the captives of Judah”?

answers: To show that the interpretation was not an ordinary human achievement
challenge.explanation: Daniel contrasted human wisdom with revelation from God.
challenge.q: Why did Daniel mention that the other wise men could not reveal the secret?

answers: God reveals what shall come to pass in the latter days
God caused the king to forget the dream
challenge.explanation: Daniel said God made known what would happen afterward.
challenge.q: What is the connection between the God of heaven and the king’s dream?

answers: They were revealed through God’s power
challenge.explanation: The revelation allowed the king to know the thoughts of his heart.
challenge.q: What did Daniel want the king to understand about the thoughts of his heart?

easy.explanation: The head was made of fine gold.
easy.q: What was the head of the image made of?

easy.explanation: The legs were made of iron.
easy.q: What were the legs made of?

easy.explanation: A stone cut without hands struck the image.
easy.q: What struck the image on its feet?

answers: Gold, silver, brass, iron, iron and clay
medium.explanation: That is the order Daniel described.
medium.q: What was the order of the materials from head to feet?

answers: They broke into pieces and were carried away by the wind
medium.explanation: They became like chaff and were carried away.
medium.q: What happened to the materials after the stone struck the image?

medium.explanation: Brass refers to a copper-like metal used in the image.
medium.q: What does the KJV word “brass” mean in this passage?

answers: The stone was made by human craftsmen
The stone was not produced by human action
The stone was part of the image
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that no human hands made the stone.
challenge.q: What does “cut out without hands” emphasize?

answers: It became a great mountain that filled the earth
challenge.explanation: The stone became a great mountain filling the whole earth.
challenge.q: What was the stone’s final result in the dream?

answers: A great and frightening image was completely broken
Smallness was contrasted with lack of color
challenge.explanation: The impressive image was utterly destroyed by the stone.
challenge.q: What striking contrast appears in the description of the image?

easy.explanation: Nebuchadnezzar was the head of gold.
easy.q: Who is represented by the head of gold?

easy.explanation: The third kingdom is represented by brass.
easy.q: Which kingdom is represented by brass?

easy.explanation: The fourth kingdom is strong as iron.
easy.q: How is the fourth kingdom described?

answers: It would be inferior to his kingdom
It would not be a kingdom
medium.explanation: Another kingdom would arise that was inferior to his.
medium.q: What would happen to the kingdom after Nebuchadnezzar’s kingdom?

answers: It is strong and breaks everything
It is made only of clay
medium.explanation: It is compared to iron that breaks and subdues all things.
medium.q: What characterizes the fourth kingdom?

medium.explanation: Inferior means lower or less excellent.
medium.q: What does “inferior” mean in “another kingdom inferior to thee”?

answers: The materials and qualities of the kingdoms change
All the kingdoms become stronger because of gold
challenge.explanation: The different materials represent different qualities and kingdoms.
challenge.q: What does the change from gold to iron suggest about the sequence of kingdoms?

answers: Divided, partly strong, and partly broken
challenge.explanation: Iron and clay represent a divided mixture of strength and weakness.
challenge.q: How is the final kingdom described in its feet and toes?

answers: They are unlike materials that do not join firmly
They were not in the feet
challenge.explanation: The passage says iron is not mixed with clay.
challenge.q: Why do iron and clay not cleave to one another?

easy.explanation: The God of heaven will set up the kingdom.
easy.q: Who will set up the kingdom described in these verses?

easy.explanation: The kingdom shall stand for ever.
easy.q: How long will this kingdom last?

easy.explanation: The stone represents the triumph of the kingdom God establishes.
easy.q: What does the stone represent?

answers: It will not be destroyed or left to another people
It will not affect other kingdoms
medium.explanation: It shall never be destroyed or handed to another people.
medium.q: What will not happen to God’s kingdom?

answers: Break them in pieces and consume them
medium.explanation: The kingdom will break in pieces and consume the other kingdoms.
medium.q: What will God’s kingdom do to the other kingdoms?

medium.explanation: It means continually and without end.
medium.q: What does “for ever” mean in this passage?

answers: The stone begins small but becomes a mountain, while the great image is broken
The image becomes a mountain and the stone disappears
challenge.explanation: The stone grows, while the image is broken and carried away.
challenge.q: What contrast is shown between the stone and the image?

answers: Daniel says the dream is certain and the interpretation sure
The gifts given by the king
challenge.explanation: Daniel explicitly calls the dream certain and the interpretation sure.
challenge.q: What supports the certainty of the dream and its interpretation?

answers: No other people will replace or seize it
Each people will possess it in turn
It will last only one generation
challenge.explanation: The statement emphasizes the kingdom’s permanence and independence.
challenge.q: What does it mean that God’s kingdom will not be left to another people?

paragraphs.title: Daniel’s Reward and His Companions’ Appointment

answers: He fell upon his face and worshipped him
He sent him away from Babylon
easy.explanation: Nebuchadnezzar fell before Daniel and worshipped him.
easy.q: What did Nebuchadnezzar do before Daniel?

answers: Many great gifts and rule over Babylon
easy.explanation: The king gave Daniel gifts and authority over the province.
easy.q: What did the king give Daniel?

easy.explanation: Daniel’s three companions were appointed over Babylon’s affairs.
easy.q: Who was appointed over the affairs of Babylon?

answers: He is God of gods and a revealer of secrets
He is only the god of war
He has no connection with the dream
medium.explanation: The king called Daniel’s God a God of gods and revealer of secrets.
medium.q: What did Nebuchadnezzar acknowledge about Daniel’s God?

answers: Ruler over the province of Babylon and chief of the governors over the wise men
medium.explanation: Daniel was made ruler and chief over Babylon’s wise men.
medium.q: What position did Daniel receive after interpreting the dream?

medium.explanation: An oblation is an offering presented in worship.
medium.q: What does the KJV word “oblation” mean?

answers: He cared about their standing and responsibilities
He wanted to distance himself from them
They refused to serve in Babylon
challenge.explanation: Daniel asked that his companions be placed over Babylon’s affairs.
challenge.q: What does Daniel’s request for his companions’ appointment show?

answers: The king promoted Daniel after recognizing that God had revealed the secret
The king promoted him before hearing the interpretation
challenge.explanation: The revelation led to honor, gifts, and Daniel’s promotion.
challenge.q: What is the connection between the king’s acknowledgment of God and Daniel’s promotion?

answers: He sat in the gate of the king
challenge.explanation: The final verse says Daniel sat in the gate of the king.
challenge.q: What important detail does the last verse give about Daniel?
